newsitem.title: USA: Auditors say NY's no-sales-tax week aids retailers.
newsitem.headline: Auditors say NY's no-sales-tax week aids retailers.

text.p: New York's "No Sales Tax Week" proved to be a boom for retailers, an auditor's survey of 102 stores said.

KPMG Peat Marwick said the New York City metropolitan area's "No Sales Tax Week" for apparel below $500 from January 17 through January 24 helped boost average sales at major chains and specialty stores by 125 percent.
KPMG Peat Marwick conducted a spot survey of 102 stores in the period.
Any move to permanently eliminate New York State's sales tax on clothing, however, would cost about $400 million in tax revenues, but it has the support of Gov. George Pataki and other officials.
New York State charges a four percent sales tax on clothing.
New York City charges an additional four percent sales tax and New York City and seven surrounding counties have an added 0.25 percent sales tax to fund the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
"Reports of some retailers' sales tripling over year-earlier figures may have raised some skepticism," Robert Dillon, KPMG's partner-in-charge of Northeast Consumer Markets, said in a statement.
"However, our spot survey shows that sales more than doubled over the same period a year ago. It was truly a promising experiment and a great time of the year to try it," Dillon said.
Dillon said later in a telephone interview that none of the retailers surveyed had indicated any unusual shopping activity in the weeks prior to the tax-free week.

Retailers told KPMG in its survey that the week-long tax moratorium also stimulated sales of non-clothing items, because of added promotions. Also, it encouraged people outside of the state to shop in New York City, KPMG said.
Several retailers also reported an increase in same store sales in New Jersey, contrary to expectations, KPMG said.
Local managers of several national retail outlets said their stores achieved the highest sales volume nationwide for their respective chains for the week, KPMG said.
